When the data knew what the stakeholder didn't

How GA4 behavioural analysis overturned a product manager's assumption about user need, and secured prioritisation for a report feature affecting 116,000+ active aviation users.

The Challenge

A feature dismissed as a minority concern

MAVIS serves thousands of aviators daily, providing real-time and forecast weather data to support safe flight planning. Central to their workflow are static weather reports: PDF-format documents produced by operational meteorologists and accessible directly through the platform.

Users had been raising complaints about these reports for months. The feedback was consistent and recurring: inability to download reports for offline use, difficulty opening reports in a new tab, font sizing issues, lack of interactivity, and problems zooming in on fine detail. These were not edge-case complaints. They were arriving daily.

"I can only see one report under each category and not the next report. Also only one chart at a time."

Private Pilot, MAVIS User Feedback

Despite the volume of feedback, the Product Manager was not confident this was the right next thing to work on. Her assumption: this is probably just one of our ten user groups pushing hard for something the rest don't need.

The tension: Qualitative feedback was present and persistent. But without data on scale, it was easy to deprioritise. The question was not whether the problem was real. It was whether it mattered to enough users to justify the investment.

Context

Ten user groups. Very unequal distribution.

MAVIS serves a range of aviation professionals across three broad categories. At the time of this research, only seven of the ten groups were actively using the platform.

The Approach

Two data sources. One argument.

GA4 Path Exploration GA4 Segment Analysis User Survey (MS Forms) Power Automate tagging Cross-functional playback Ideation session

I designed a two-strand approach: systematic collection and classification of qualitative feedback running in parallel with independent GA4 behavioural analysis. The aim was not to use one to illustrate the other, but to run both independently and see whether they converged on the same conclusion.

1

Built a structured feedback pipeline

Configured a Microsoft Forms survey to capture ongoing user feedback. Used Power Automate to auto-populate and classify responses in SharePoint, tagging each submission by user group, feature area, device, and feedback type.

2

Filtered to surface the reports signal

Filtered the SharePoint tracker to surface all feedback tagged area: static-reports. The spread across user groups was immediately visible. Feedback was not clustering in one group.

3

Ran GA4 segment overlap analysis

Created defined user segments in GA4 for General Aviation Users and Helicopter Users and ran a segment overlap comparison to establish the actual size of each active group. This directly tested the PM's assumption.

4

Ran path exploration from report_click

Built a path exploration in GA4 using report_click as the starting event to understand which reports were being accessed, how frequently, and what journeys users were taking after clicking into them.

5

Playback and ideation session

Synthesised both data sources into a single playback for the PM, Delivery Manager, Business Manager, and wider team. The session moved directly from evidence to a committed ideation sprint.

The Evidence

Four screenshots. One overturned assumption.

Platform scale: 115K active users, 2.3M events in 28 days

The GA4 Reports Snapshot established the baseline. MAVIS had 115,000 active users in the 28-day window with an average engagement time of 4 minutes 10 seconds. This is a high-frequency operational platform, not a niche tool.

GA4 Reports Snapshot · 28-day window May 12 to Jun 8, 2026 · 115K active users, 2.3M events

Qualitative signal: reports feedback spans every active user group

The SharePoint feedback tracker showed feedback tagged area: static-reports coming from Gliders, Balloonists, Private Pilots, Microlights, Offshore Helicopter Pilots, and Instructors. This was not one user group raising a complaint. It was the entire active user base.

MAVIS User Feedback Meta Data · auto-populated via Power Automate · filtered to area: static-reports

Segment analysis: GA users are 99.4% of the active base

The GA4 segment overlap made the most critical point simply. General Aviation Users numbered 116,217. Helicopter Users numbered 737. Zero overlap. The group the PM thought was a minority was the overwhelming majority of the entire active user population.

GA4 Segment Overlap · General Aviation Users (116,217) vs Helicopter Users (737) · zero overlap confirmed
116,217 General Aviation active users
737 Helicopter active users
99.4% Of active users in the so-called minority group
157:1 Ratio of GA to Helicopter users

27,825 report_click events across all major report types

The path exploration from report_click showed 27,825 total events. F214 and F215 each received over 7,800 clicks. Reports were not peripheral: they were among the most accessed features on the platform.

GA4 Path Exploration · Starting event: report_click · 27,825 total events · breakdown by report type

Key Insights

Three things the data made undeniable

Insight 01

The assumption about user group distribution was wrong by a factor of 157

GA4 segment analysis showed General Aviation users outnumbered Helicopter users 157:1 and made up 99.4% of the entire active base. The minority was not a minority. It was almost everyone.

Insight 02

27,825 report interactions proved this was a core workflow, not an edge case

Users were navigating directly to report pages repeatedly within established sessions. F214 and F215 were two of the highest-trafficked features on the platform. Improving reports was maintenance of a critical daily workflow.

Insight 03

Feedback volume understated the scale of the problem

Users who submitted feedback represented only a fraction of users engaging with reports. The 27,825 behavioural interactions dwarfed the complaint volume, meaning the silent majority were experiencing the same friction but not raising it.

What I'd do differently

I would establish GA4 segment definitions for all ten user groups from the start of the product lifecycle, not reactively when a prioritisation question arises. Having pre-defined, maintained segments would make this kind of analysis available as a standing resource for the whole team, not something built from scratch when a specific question lands.
